title: "Risk and issues register"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-31"

Use this register for decision-relevant uncertainty and current problems, not as a warehouse for every worry. Read [Risks, blocked work and change](../chapters/part-09/26-risks-blocked-change.qmd) before first use.

## Classification key

- **Risk:** an uncertain future event or condition.
- **Issue:** the event has happened or the condition exists.
- **Waiting:** progress depends on a known external action.
- **Blocked:** the current route cannot produce the required outcome.
- **Incident:** harm, breach, loss or unsafe conduct may have occurred; use the authorised urgent process.

## Blank register

| ID | State | Cause, event and consequence | Current evidence | Prevention or current response | Contingency or alternative | Owner | Trigger, follow-up or escalation date | Status and closure evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-001 | risk / issue / waiting / blocked | Because [cause], [event] may/has occurred, causing [consequence] | known: [ ]; uncertain: [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [date + condition] | open / monitoring / escalated / closed because [evidence] |

If likelihood or consequence ratings are required locally, define the scale beside the register. Do not present guessed numbers as measured probability.

## Contingency card for a consequential risk

Complete one card for any risk that could make a study infeasible, threaten an important deadline or interrupt a duty of care. Attach it to the matching register ID.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Register ID and protected outcome | [What must remain possible or protected?] |
| Trigger | [Observable condition or date that prompts a decision] |
| Fallback route | [Specific alternative, including what it can and cannot answer] |
| Test before activation | [Small check that shows whether the fallback is feasible] |
| Activation owner | [Person who can decide to switch] |
| Required authority | [Ethics, governance, data, safety, partner, funder or candidature decision, if any] |
| Prerequisites | [Approval, access, skill, equipment, code, budget or handover needed] |
| Review date | [When the trigger and fallback will be reconsidered] |
| Activation record | [Decision, date, reason and linked approval] |
| Evidence that the fallback works | [Test, access confirmation, restore result, calibration or other proof] |

### Worked contingency card: recruitment is slower than planned

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Register ID and protected outcome | R-007; retain a study capable of answering the approved comparison question |
| Trigger | fewer than 24 eligible approaches and eight enrolments by the six-week review, with 12 recruitment weeks remaining |
| Fallback route | assess a second approved site and a lower-burden appointment schedule; if neither can recover the required information, take a redesign or stop recommendation to the supervisory and ethics routes |
| Test before activation | confirm the second site's eligible pool, staff capacity, data compatibility and governance route; estimate recruitment from observed screening figures |
| Activation owner | principal investigator recommends; the student prepares evidence; the responsible ethics, site and candidature authorities decide within their remits |
| Required authority | written site permission and any required ethics or governance amendment before recruitment changes |
| Prerequisites | trained recruiter, approved materials, secure data route and revised timetable |
| Review date | week six, then fortnightly if the approved second site is activated |
| Activation record | [decision link, date and version of the approved recruitment plan] |
| Evidence that the fallback works | observed screening, enrolment and retention figures compared with the dated threshold |

Do not treat this worked example as a universal recruitment rule. Its numbers are illustrative; the design, approved protocol and local process determine the real threshold and authority.

| ID | State | Cause, event and consequence | Current evidence | Prevention or current response | Contingency or alternative | Owner | Trigger, follow-up or escalation date | Status and closure evidence |

| R-004 | issue; analysis waiting | Because partner legal review has no decision date, the controlled-data extract was not confirmed by 15 Sep, which may make the primary analysis infeasible in candidature | request acknowledged; variable list and approval absent; no transfer | request written timetable; test pipeline with synthetic data | assess public dataset and narrower question; prepare change decision | student: tests and record; supervisor: scientific decision; custodian: access | follow up 18 Sep; choose route 30 Sep | open; closes only with written access or approved alternative and updated records |

## Review procedure

At each agreed review:

1. confirm the state from current evidence;
2. convert a risk to an issue when its trigger occurs;
3. test whether waiting has become blocked;
4. complete or escalate due actions;
5. activate contingencies before the protected buffer is exhausted;
6. link any material change to the decision record and required approval; and
7. close only with observable evidence.

## Scenario test

The access trigger passes without confirmation. The correct response is not to copy the row into next week's register unchanged. Reclassify it as an issue, execute the named follow-up, test the alternative and take a decision by the recorded threshold.

If the custodian later approves a smaller variable set, do not simply close the issue. First determine whether the reduced data alter the question, method, ethics, analysis or contribution. Record and approve the resulting change where required.

## Privacy and authority boundary

Record the project consequence and response. Keep sensitive personal, participant, health, misconduct or case details in the authorised confidential process. This register does not replace incident, safety, privacy, ethics or research-integrity reporting.

## Evidence to retain

- dated register versions or change history;
- consequential requests and responses;
- test results supporting alternatives;
- linked decisions and approvals;
- revised plans or protocols; and
- closure evidence.
